uniequip_002_narant:
Narantuya wakes from the dream with a start. She feels as though she has a piece of smouldering charcoal in her throat, and all she can hear is the unbearable clanging of metal that filled her dream.
She walks out of the tent. There is no moon in the sky, and the wind blows towards the depths of the desert like galloping cavalrymen.
'Clank! Clank!' The sound of metal banging on metal keeps getting louder. Narantuya looks around her, trying to find the source of the sound, only to discover that the black scimitar on her belt is vibrating violently.
She grabs the hilt, hoping to stop the movement, only for it to vibrate even harder, causing her arm to go numb and her eyes to see stars.
'Stop!' She roars, clutching the blade even harder.
The black scimitar drags her stumbling into the night.
She sees a hammer the size of a mountain slamming upon a red-hot anvil. The metal screams along the distant drums of war, sending golden sparks flying like drops of sweat. The hammer scorns ordinary iron and turns the indestructible anvil into a scimitar!
The war drums grow closer. She sees someone take the scimitar and walk at the front of an expedition, cutting through bones and tattered banners. Then at some point, the wielder dies, and the scimitar falls to the sand. Narantuya realizes that they are the same sands she now stands upon.
'...No,' she says, 'That's not me!'
No longer trying to stop the blade's restlessness, she throws it with all her might, as though trying to smash the mirage in the sandstorm.
'I don't care who you are! I walk my own path! If you do not wish to accompany me, then so be it!'
Narantuya is unsure if she actually said those words, because the very next instant she stumbles and falls to the sand.
...
Narantuya awakens to find her drinking buddies fanning her, half-concerned, half-fearful.
'Was I drunk?'
The stall owner doesn't answer. He smiles and continues his work, mixing the booze with water.
'Where's my sword?!' Narantuya reaches towards her belt and breaks out in a cold sweat.
Her drinking buddies lead her to a great rock.
'How the heck did you even do this, Narantuya?'
She rubs her eyes. Yes, it is her black scimitar alright, buried inside the rock all the way to the hilt. She tries to pull it out, but neither sword nor rock budge in the slightest.
'There was a bit of thunder last night. You came out of your tent, looking a little tipsy, and cussed out the clouds before drawing your sword and swinging it at the rock, just like that!' One of her drinking buddies says, 'You scared the living daylights out of me. I'll pay back the drinking money I owe you today...'
'You were scary alright. I remember that you yelled—'
'Yelled what?' The memory is coming back. She is pleasantly surprised that she managed to come up with a declaration so powerful, and would not mind hearing it again from someone else.
'You yelled—'I'll trade you in for one made of gold if you don't stay put!''
'What? Wait, shouldn't it be—'
'Yeah, that was it. I heard it too. Definitely sounds like something you'd say, Narantuya.'
'...'
uniequip_003_narant:
'She's no good!'
The two runaway girls were lost in the wilds, the sky darkening above them, every direction the same as the last.
'That red-haired lunatic only took us off the desert bandits so she could sell us on to some other desert bandits!'
Ayaji and Ayani were not sisters by blood, but slaves the desert bandits had seized from different places; even their names were ones they had given themselves.
'But she cut off our shackles, and she gives us food.'
'It's an act! She's always going on about the rules of some tribe or other—all so we'll let our guard down.'
'Ayaji, I can't walk anymore! I want to go back. At least we don't go hungry with her.'
'Even if you're going to be a desert bandit, you'd want a boss who's going somewhere, wouldn't you? Look at the state of her—she doesn't have a single underling. What kind of future is that?'
'But she said she used to have plenty of underlings. They just all stopped wanting to run with her, so she decided she'd never be anyone's boss again.'
'Then why don't you stop and think about why none of them wanted to run with her?'
So caught up were they in their quarrel that they never noticed the pack of roaming manglerbeasts that had crept up on them.
'Th-this is bad! Ayaji, I don't want to die out here!'
The manglerbeast matriarch circled the two of them as though waiting for something. The rest of the pack began to howl into the distance. Before long, a red figure appeared.
'Didn't I tell you there were manglerbeasts about? Didn't I tell you not to go wandering off while I was out buying supplies?'
'I thought you were just trying to scare us out of running away!'
'Running away? Go whenever you like. When have I ever stopped you?'
Panting for breath, Narantuya handed the whip and the dagger to the two of them, then stepped forward, and the game of predator and prey became a standoff between two packs.
'You have your pack to keep alive. So do I. These two are mine. We will fight back, and I will kill the manglerbeasts in your pack—three of them, two of them, that many I can kill for certain. If mutual ruin is what you want, then let's have it.'
The manglerbeast matriarch fell silent.
'Not worth the price, is it?' Narantuya spat on the ground. 'Then get lost!'
The enraged manglerbeasts roared one after another, and Narantuya threw back her head and roared right back at them, answering them with an attitude of her own.
Only when every last manglerbeast had drawn in its fangs did she stop. She tossed out a parcel she had only just bought: inside was the salt the pack could not do without.
The matriarch took the parcel of salt in her jaws and led the pack back into the depths of the wastes.
'Come on. We're going home.' Narantuya's voice had gone hoarse. 'I've taken you on as my underlings, so from here on you do as I say. No more wandering off.'
'W-when did you take us on as underlings? And weren't you never going to be anyone's boss again?'
'Can't be helped. I don't want to be a boss either, but I can hardly stand around and watch the two of you die, can I? If you don't like it, I can always call the manglerbeasts back.'
Ayaji shut her mouth. Ayani leaned in and whispered, 'This boss just scared off a whole pack of manglerbeasts. She's definitely going places.'
Ayaji sighed. 'We both owe her our lives now. How are we ever supposed to repay that? We can't very well be her underlings for the rest of our days.'
'Ayaji, that's the second time she's saved us. The rest of our days might not even be enough.'
Without so much as turning her head, Narantuya answered, 'I don't need repaying, and I haven't the patience to be anybody's boss for the rest of my life either! Someday we'll go our separate ways, and once you're living somewhere safe and settled, it's enough that you remember me. Better still if you're willing to post me a little something on the holidays.'
'Don't you worry, boss! We'll send you the finest presents there are!'
'...There's no need to be in quite such a hurry to plan for after we've split up.'
